entries.capability: Load and parse APEXlang exports declaring mmdVersion 26.2.0+3479
entries.notes: All 33 real apps on oracle/apex's 26.2 branch (commit fbe095e) load and parse with zero throws; the only parser warnings are the 3 raw-TAB cases (see parser-raw-tab-in-quoted-string-26-2). The 26.1 and 26.2 EBNFs were diffed production by production (12 added, 118 removed, 224 changed of which 159 are pure reorderings); none of the removed or changed productions maps to a typed field this parser projects. The same 33 apps from the 26.1 branch were compared entity by entity: only pageAccessProtection and switch-item `required` change systematically. STATIC parsing only -- no runtime claim.

supportMatrixRow.how: All 33 parse with zero throws; EBNF 26.1 vs 26.2 diffed production by production and the same 33 apps compared across releases -- see docs/grammar-assumptions.md "APEX 26.2 compatibility". Static parsing only; no runtime behaviour was verified on 26.2

entries.capability: Meaning of an omitted security.pageAccessProtection in a 26.2 export
entries.notes: 1,490 pages paired across oracle/apex 26.1 and 26.2: 1,431 went argumentsMustHaveChecksum -> omitted, 13 omitted -> unrestricted, 17 noArgumentsSupported unchanged; 26.2 writes argumentsMustHaveChecksum explicitly on zero pages. The EBNF production is identical in both releases and states no default, so 'omitted means argumentsMustHaveChecksum on 26.2' is an inference from export data, not an Oracle statement and not live-confirmed. Implemented as a flagged default (ApexPage.pageAccessProtectionDefaulted), never applied to page 0, 26.2 manifests only. It is the fail-safe reading (assuming unrestricted would generate tests that redirect to /login). Upgrade to verified with a live 26.2 run, or an Oracle statement of the default.

supportMatrixRow.verifiedAgainst: Inferred from 1,490 paired pages across oracle/apex 26.1 vs 26.2 (static)
supportMatrixRow.how: 26.2 omits `argumentsMustHaveChecksum` where 26.1 wrote it; the parser resolves an omitted value to it for 26.2 only (flagged `pageAccessProtectionDefaulted`, never page 0). An inference from export data -- not stated by Oracle and not live-confirmed

entries.capability: Raw TAB character inside a quoted string value
entries.notes: 3 raw TABs in 2 real apps, present on both the oracle/apex 26.1 and 26.2 branches; 0 other raw control characters across 2,350 (26.1) / 2,961 (26.2) .apx files. The EBNF references <string_character> but never defines it, so real data decides (ADR-004). Only TAB is tolerated; any other control character still raises 'Invalid quoted string'. Not a 26.2 regression: on the pre-change code generate() refused both apps on the 26.1 branch too.

26.1 exports write `validation { valueRequired: true }` on switch items; 26.2 omits the group, so ApexItem.required reads true -> false on 60 items in 8 apps (raw text compared for poll P19_ANONYMOUS_YN). The parser reports the export faithfully. `required` feeds only apx-diff, apx-docs and a comment in generated page objects, never an assertion, so an upgrade diff lists these items as changed but no generated test is affected.

entries.capability: SQLcl `apex validate` invocation and success detection on 26.2
entries.notes: SQLcl 26.2's User's Guide (12.1.3) still documents -input as optional ('If omitted, the current directory is used') and lists `apex validate` with no arguments as an example -- the form apx-onboard runs (sql /nolog @script, cwd = the export). Oracle's own 26.2 apexlang-compile script (oracle/skills) uses the explicit -input form, requires the literal 'Validation successful' marker and notes SQLcl can report errors while exiting 0 -- the same fail-closed rule apx-onboard applies, so no code change was made. oracle/skills PR #133 reports SQLcl needs the FULL mmdVersion build and that SQLcl 26.1.2 rejects 26.2 apps with INVALID_VERSION (the PR author's test result, not Oracle documentation). Not executed here: no SQLcl 26.2 and no database were available in this pass.

supportMatrixRow.verifiedAgainst: SQLcl 26.2 User's Guide + Oracle's 26.2 validate script (documentation), not run here
supportMatrixRow.how: The invocation apx-onboard uses (`apex validate` with the export as working directory) is documented for SQLcl 26.2, and the `Validation successful` fail-closed rule matches Oracle's own script. Use a SQLcl at least as new as the export; SQLcl 26.1.2 is reported to reject 26.2 apps (INVALID_VERSION). Not executed in this pass
